title: Common Water Heater Myths Answered: Reading Plates, Extending Life, Draining, and Leaks

summary: This Old House’s water heater primer addresses common homeowner questions about when to replace, how to evaluate the equipment, and practical maintenance. The video explains how to identify tank size, model, and age from the rating plate, contrasts electric and gas units, and notes typical lifespans for glass-lined steel tanks. It covers the sacrificial anode rod and how replacing it can extend life, debunks the notion that periodic draining alone will dramatically prolong service, and demonstrates a drainage procedure to flush sediment. It also provides a safety-focused leak response (shut off cold water, relieve pressure) and discusses the real-world tradeoffs of upgrading to a tankless system, including the higher piping and installation demands. Location context is provided via a basement and a first-floor example to illustrate risk considerations depending on where the heater lives in a house.
